Information since June points to continued labor-market strength and real activity growing at a strong pace, with inflation and longer-run expectations near 2 percent. In standard New Keynesian frameworks with nominal rigidities (e.g., Gali; Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005), well-anchored expectations justify gradual rate increases to limit output and employment volatility. The statement’s “balanced risks” and accommodative stance are also consistent with the credit/banking transmission of monetary policy to the real economy (Bernanke and Mihov 1998; Curdia and Woodford 2008), while low unemployment alongside strong growth aligns with Okun’s law. In expansion, reserve demand typically rises, matching the Desk’s operational guidance. Overall tone: positive growth outlook with cautious, data-dependent normalization.
